subject: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up (Acme)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up (Acme)

Hi Alyssa — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and next steps so we don't lose momentum: \n\n- Key goals: reduce customer support handle time by 30% using an in-product assistant; preserve PII redaction and auditability.\n- Top KPIs: avg handle time, escalation rate, quality/regression on top-10 intents.\n- Current constraints: sensitive fields (SSN, account numbers), short-turnaround SLA (sub-200ms for top-tier routes).\n\nAction items we discussed:\n1) You to share a representative prompt set (customer-facing prompts + edge cases) and any internal redaction guidance.\n2) We will run a model-fit eval (benchmarks + prompt-set pass/fail) and recommend model/quantization profiles.\n3) If results look good, schedule a focused eval demo with your engineering/security teams next week.\n\nCan you attach the prompt CSV you mentioned and any redaction notes? Preferably anonymized but keep edge cases so we can test worst-case behavior. If you need a template, I attached a very small example.\n\nThanks — I’ll loop Logan in for evaluation logistics.\n\u2014\nMarissa Cole\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\nmarissa@redwood.com\n--Attachment: prompt_template_example.csv (text/csv)

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Data Privacy <privacy@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up (Acme)

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary, this looks right. Attached the prompt set we pulled together and our redaction notes. A couple of context notes:\n\n- The prompt CSV includes three columns: "prompt_id", "user_prompt", "expected_action/context". We redacted actual account IDs but left formats (e.g., XXXX-XXXX) and edge cases like embedded PII in free text.\n- Our privacy team flagged: prefer deterministic redaction for account numbers and an audit trail for any de-anonymization requests. See the PDF for our recommended redaction rules.\n- We included 20 edge-case prompts where the user includes mixed sensitive tokens (phone + partial SSN). Those are the ones we most want you to stress-test.\n\nAttachments:\n- acme_prompt_set_v1.csv (text/csv)\n- acme_edgecases_redaction_notes.pdf (application/pdf)\n\nHappy to hop on a follow-up to walk through any of the examples.\n\nBest,\nAlyssa Turner\nProduct Manager, Acme Corp\nalyssa.turner@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up (Acme)

Thanks Alyssa — received both files and the redaction notes. Quick responses and proposed next steps: \n\n1) Model recommendations for initial eval (based on requirements: latency, cost, and redaction safety):\n   - For hosted pilot: redwood/gpt-medium-eco (quantized) — good balance of latency/cost for short-turnaround routes.\n   - For higher accuracy on complex edge cases: redwood/gpt-large-v2 (fp16 or int8) — we can run an A/B on a small percentage of traffic.\n\n2) Benchmark & eval plan:\n   - We’ll run prompt-set coverage tests, a confusion matrix for top intents, and targeted redaction stress tests.\n   - Benchmarks & initial results will be uploaded here: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/llm-fit-acme-2026\n\n3) Redaction handling: we’ll test both pre-response masking (recommended for PII) and post-response filter layers. If you can confirm whether you prefer masking-only vs. audit/reable flow, we’ll tailor the eval.\n\n4) Logistics: Logan, can you run the prompt-set eval and share a short report by EOD Wednesday? Ben — can you prepare quantization profile suggestions if we need to move to int8?\n\nAlyssa — can you also share a Google Drive link with any additional prompt variants (especially multi-turn snippets)? If there are legal/PII constraints, we’ll only use the sanitized CSV you provided unless privacy approves otherwise.\n\nNext steps for us after the eval: recommend model + rollout policy, estimate cost delta, and propose a canary plan.\n\nThanks —\nMarissa\n--\nMarissa Cole\nAccount Executive, Redwood Inference\nmarissa@redwood.com

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Prompt collection & model-fit follow-up (Acme)

On it — I’ll kick off the eval job now against redwood/gpt-medium-eco and redwood/gpt-large-v2. Plan:\n\n- Smoke test (sanity & latency) on a 100-sample subset by lunchtime.\n- Full prompt-set run overnight (coverage + redaction stress tests).\n- Upload results + confusion matrix to the Drive link and ping Alyssa for any follow-ups.\n\nHubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/RDW-ACME-2026-04\n\u2014Logan\nSenior ML Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference\nlogan@redwood.com
